The host saves it once the person pauses for `data-debounce` milliseconds (1 000 when it is left out, held to 250–10 000), at once when they leave the field, and as the view goes, whatever was still waiting. `data-save="change"` saves on the field's `change` alone. A save is a press in every way but the click: the act is the field's own `data-act`, its record and its fieldset's fields are read as a press reads them and held to the same rules — only what the person typed, a prefilled value only back where it came from, under their grants — and a click into the field is not a press.

### Hearing what became of it

The press applies before the view hears it, so the view never decides whether it happened: a bound press's `click` carries `event.pressed`, and every act a press or a save asked for comes back as an `acted` event on the bound element, `event.pressed` holding `as`, `ok`, and `reason` and `message` when it was refused:

```js
graview.on("input", "textarea", () => draw("Saving…"));
graview.on("acted", "textarea", (e) => draw(e.pressed.ok ? "Saved" : e.pressed.message));
```

Say the refusal's `message` as it is: it is the policy's sentence, or the host's. `examples/a-call-sheet.js` is a whole one: a call's notes, filled by the host, saved as they are typed, "Saving…" on `input` and "Saved" on `acted`.

### Then find out whether it worked

1. `graview check` the app the view writes to: a form is only as sound as the acts it asks for. `checkManifest(manifest, store)` from `@graview/guest/host/views` must say nothing; it refuses an act the app does not declare.
2. Run it headless as a member who may see less than you: `graview view check view.js --app <app> --manifest manifest.json --seed <seed.json> --roles <role>`. It reports `act` for an act its manifest does not name, and says when a field's `data-save` would save nothing: no `data-act` or `name`, no fieldset bound to a record, a `data-save` other than `input` or `change`, a `data-debounce` it does not read, or a `data-save` on what is not a field, or a `data-act` on what can never be pressed.
3. Press it headless: `--press "<selector>"` (with `--type note="…"` for what the person typed), or `runWorkerViewHeadless(…, { press: { selector, typed } })`. It presses the first element the selector matches and says what the host would do: the act and the arguments it carries, and whether this seat may (rehearsed, never applied), or the refusal the view would hear; the link it follows; and what the view's code did on the click.
4. Open it on both faces as that member, and on a phone. Press each with typed words, then again with a field the view filled. The first applies and the second is refused. A prefilled field is filled only for a seat that may write it: open it as one who may not, and it is empty.
5. Type into a field that saves, stop, and see "Saved"; type again and leave it at once, and see the save land without the pause.

### What the check cannot see

`graview check` judges the declaration, not the form. It cannot see a field named for the wrong argument, a button that says "Save" over an act that sends, or a view that says "Saved" without waiting for `acted`. A headless run presses once, when asked, and lets no pause pass, so it cannot see a save land or a press that a field covers; only pressing and typing on the faces, on a phone too, as a seat with narrow sight, does. Nor can it see a form that asks for what the person should not have to type.

---

Let a Graview worker view change records — a bound press (data-act), the fields a person types into, a record's own text filled to edit (data-prefill), a field that saves as it is typed (data-save) and the view hearing what became of each act (acted) — and prove a press applies and a field the view filled is refused, rather than assuming the form works.

The page: https://graview.dev/docs/skills/graview-view-forms.html · Every Graview docs page, for a model: https://graview.dev/llms.txt

---

Source: https://graview.dev/docs/skills/graview-view-links.html

# graview-view-links

`graview-view-links` is one of Graview's 30 authoring skills: instructions an AI coding assistant such as Claude Code or Codex reads before it changes a Graview app. What it teaches: Send a person from a Graview worker view to a record, a place or a list — an <a data-record>, or a whole card or row bound to a record that opens on a click, a phone's tap and Enter — narrowed and to a section, and prove each lands by pressing it on a phone as well as a desk rather than assuming a card the describer lists opens.

Installed into a project by `graview skills install .`, and read by whichever assistant is working beside you.

## The skill

## Links in a worker view

A worker view (`graview-worker-view`: its manifest, its global, its limits) writes no address of the page's: an `href` it built is never drawn. What it may link to is a record, a named place or a kind's list of this app, and the host makes that a link and follows it, on both faces, only to what the viewer may see.

**Go somewhere with a link, do something with a button.** `<a data-record>` or `<a data-place>` to go; `<button>`, or `<button data-act>` (`graview-view-forms`), to do. Style both as you like: the host resets a button and a link it made to the words around them at no specificity, so your own class always wins. A `<div>` or `<span>` with a `graview.on("click")` handler is reached by no keyboard and is nothing to a screen reader: do not draw one. A list of records is a list of `<a data-record>`, never `graview.on("click", "[data-id]", … navigate)`.

### A link

`<a data-record="offer:7">` and `<a data-place="the-packages">` are links the host follows. On the routed pages the host gives each the address it goes to as its `href` (`/a/<app>/offers/offer%3A7`), so it shows on hover, copies, and opens in a new tab on Cmd- or Ctrl-click or a middle click; a plain click, a tap and Enter stay in the app. On the scene, which has no addresses, it is given the keyboard and a link's role instead — and so in an embed whose host keeps its own addresses (memory routing), unless the host says its address for a page with the embed's `hrefOf`. A `<button data-record>` goes there too. `<a href>` goes out only to an address a record was handed — its own url, `mailto:`, `tel:` (below). A destination is a record's id, else a place by its slug or its title (`data-place="songs-by-writer"` or `"Songs by writer"`), else a kind's list (`features` or `feature`); any other says why, naming the places. A titled view of many is a place too, at `/places/<its title as a slug>`: `data-place="live-threats"` reaches the view "Live threats", and the check knows it when its host hands the views it keeps. From code, `graview.navigate("offer:7")` goes by the same rules.

In SVG the same `<a data-record>` is a link — a timeline's dot, a map's pin — with its address, the keyboard and Enter: `<svg role="group" aria-label="…"><a data-record="amendment:19" aria-label="19th, 1920"><circle …/></a></svg>`. It takes no `href` of yours; a link out is an HTML one.

### Links out

`<a href="${node.url}">` is drawn where the address is one a record the view was shown holds, as it holds it — an `https:` page, a `mailto:`, a `tel:` — or an `https:` address on an origin the host lists (`links: { origins }` on the view's definition and a headless run). The host opens it in a new tab, no opener, no referrer, marked ↗. An address you build, `javascript:`, `data:` or `http:` is refused: a link a view made could carry what it reads out.

### A card that opens

Any element with `data-record` or `data-place` is a link, not only an `<a>`. Put an `<a>` to the same record on its heading:

```html
<div class="card" data-record="threat:7">
  <h3><a data-record="threat:7">Invoice phishing</a></h3>
  <span class="badge">critical</span><span class="badge">new</span>
  <p>Forty mailboxes got the fake invoice.</p>
  <button data-more="threat:7">More</button>
</div>
```

The heading's `<a>` is the keyboard's and the screen reader's link; the card, a `<div>` or an `<li>` alike, takes no role and no tab stop of its own, and is a bigger target: the host draws it with a pointer, `touch-action: manipulation` and a faint tap highlight, and follows it on a click and a phone's tap anywhere inside it — its heading, a badge, a line — unless the press lands on something with a press of its own: a button, a field, a `data-act`, a lightbox, a drop target, a control's `role`, another link. So "More" above toggles and opens nothing, and the audit finds no link inside a link. A card with no such `<a>` is given the keyboard and `role="link"` itself (a list's item keeps its role; a table's row gives the keyboard to its first cell); then it may hold no button, and a heading that links elsewhere is a link inside a link.

It is no link when it is a press scope: a `fieldset` or `role="group"` (the record a form's acts are done to), an element with `data-act`, `data-lightbox`, `data-drop` or `data-field`, a field, or an element that holds a field to type into or pick from (a checkbox inside leaves its row a link). Link such a card's title instead: `<h3><a data-record="…">`.

Do not work around it: no `data-open` with `graview.on("click", …, graview.navigate)`, no `pointer-events: none` on a card's children, no `touch-action` of your own. A card that should do something of its own on a press carries `data-key`, not `data-record`, and `graview.on`.

### How a tap reaches the view

A phone makes a tap a `click` on what the finger landed on; iOS does so only on what looks pressable, which is why the host draws every link with a pointer. The host hears it on the view's shadow root, follows a link first, then tells the view, which hears `click` as it hears a mouse's: `graview.on("click", ".card", (e) => …)` is handed `e.target`, what the finger landed on, and `e.element`, the element the selector matched at or above it, so a tap on a card's heading hands the card.

### Narrowed, and to a section

A list or a lens may be gone to **narrowed**: `where: { stage: "building" }` in navigate, `data-filter="stage:building"` on a link — the words the list's own arranging line writes, so the address is `/features?filter= stage%3Abuilding` and can be shared. A lens narrows the records it is handed; a blocks lens lists what its own `where` says. Any destination may take a **section**, a heading's words or an element's id (`section: "Every feature"`, `data-section`): the page scrolls there and gives it the keyboard (`#every-feature`). On the scene a list is the kind's stop narrowed (`in.filter`); a section is looked for there too. A filter on a field the kind lacks, or a choice it lacks, goes nowhere and says why (`Features have no field "stag" to filter by; they filter by …`), so link to the list narrowed rather than to a lens per filter; a lens kept only as a link target can be hidden (set-lens-hidden, `graview-pages`).

### Then find out whether it worked

1. `graview check` the app the view links into: a link is only as sound as the records and places it names.
2. `graview view check view.js --app <app> --manifest manifest.json --seed <seed.json> --roles <role>` says every `data-record` or `data-place` that names nothing the seat was shown and no place, and every filter that goes nowhere. `--press ".card h3"` presses there and says where the host would go, or that the press is a button's of its own. `--audit` holds what it drew to the keyboard and screen-reader rules, as the host draws it: a `<div>` heard only by `graview.on("click")`, a control or link with no name, a toggle with no state, a button inside a card that opens, an `<img>` with no alt. Each comes with its WCAG criterion and a one-line fix, and the check fails on what the view must fix. Contrast, the ring and a keyboard trap need a browser: add `--browser` (the project's Playwright and its Chromium) to run them.
3. Open it on a phone, 390 pixels wide with touch: tap a card's heading and a badge inside it, and see the record's page; tap a toggle inside it, and see it toggle and stay. On a desk, Tab through the view: every link and button is reached, with a ring; Enter on a card opens it, and Cmd-click on an `<a data-record>` opens it in a new tab.
4. Follow each link narrowed and to a section, and see it land where it says.

### What the check cannot see

`graview check` judges the declaration, not the view. A headless run lays nothing out, so it cannot see a card covered by something drawn over it, a link too small to tap, or a card that looks like it opens and holds a field. Only tapping it on a phone does. Nor can it see a link that goes somewhere true but unhelpful.

---

Send a person from a Graview worker view to a record, a place or a list — an <a data-record>, or a whole card or row bound to a record that opens on a click, a phone's tap and Enter — narrowed and to a section, and prove each lands by pressing it on a phone as well as a desk rather than assuming a card the describer lists opens.

The page: https://graview.dev/docs/skills/graview-view-links.html · Every Graview docs page, for a model: https://graview.dev/llms.txt

---

Source: https://graview.dev/docs/skills/graview-view-specs.html

# graview-view-specs

`graview-view-specs` is one of Graview's 30 authoring skills: instructions an AI coding assistant such as Claude Code or Codex reads before it changes a Graview app. What it teaches: Say how a Graview kind's card, row and page read, as data — blocks from a closed set bound by {field} templates and rule-language conditions, headlines, figures and lists of related records — and the values worked out from others (computed) that they show, verified by graview check and the page rather than by assuming the spec drew.

Installed into a project by `graview skills install .`, and read by whichever assistant is working beside you.

## The skill

## A kind's views, as data

A kind declared is drawn already: a card, a row, a page. When that default is wrong but a component would be too much, say the card, the row and the page as data. Nothing in a spec runs, so a chat can write one as safely as a person, and every face draws the same words from it. The kind itself — fields, edges, label, roles — is `graview-node-kind`.

### Do this

1. **Say the card, the row and the page** in `defineApp({ viewSpecs })` — blocks from a closed set, bound by `{field}` templates and rule-language conditions:

```ts viewSpecs: { fixture: { card: [{ title: "{name}" }, { badge: "{status}", tone: { expr: "if(status == 'fitted', 'good', 'neutral')" } }, { field: "cost", as: "money" }], row: [{ title: "{name}" }, { badge: "{status}" }], page: [{ progress: { value: "done", max: "total" }, label: "Fitted" }], } } ```

In a document the same is the top-level `views.<kind>`, and the edit is `{ "op": "set-view", "kind": "fixture", "slot": "card", "blocks": [...] }` (`null` gives the default back).

`card` is drawn beside the focus and on the pages face's gallery, `row` as the one line a member is among many (a focused group, the list page), and `page` above the default record. Tones are `good`, `warn`, `bad`, `neutral` and `accent`, the theme's own. A card shows three lines of a `text` block and a row one; `{ text: "{awards}", lines: 6 }` shows six, `lines: 0` the text whole (`view-lines` refuses past 12). Nothing in a spec runs: no CSS, no markup, and the only link drawn is an http(s) `url` field's own value, or a listed record. The scaffold's `views()` draws them (`registerViewSpecs`); so does the embed, by itself.

A row is a link to its record, so it is always named: one whose blocks show no `title`, no `headline` and no words holding the record's whole name (`{severity} · {status}` alone) is drawn with the name first, and `describe_place` says it so. Lead with `{ "title": "{name}" }` to choose how the name reads.

A kind that also has a worker view of one record draws, on its record page, the view, then the `page` blocks, then the facts they did not say. A view whose manifest says `replaces: "page"` is the whole page: the `page` blocks are never drawn, and `describePlace`, told the host's views, says so as a problem (`shadowedPageSlots`, `@graview/core/describe`). Draw what they said in the view, or leave `replaces` out.

1. **Say more with three blocks** (FR-81, FR-82): `{ headline: "{count(out('includes'))} offers" }`; `{ figure: "net", as: "money", label: "{name}, net" }` (`number`, `money`, `percent`; the label is a template; `figure: true` is still the picture); and

```ts { list: "out('includes')", as: "row", sort: { by: "net", direction: "desc" }, limit: 5, group: { by: "type", headings: { pain: "What hurts" } }, empty: "None yet." } ```

— records by a walk or `all('kind')`, each drawn by its own card or row and a link; `direction: "choices"` is a choice's declared order. Lists show only what the seat sees, and nest three deep, then say names. The same blocks write the home (`views.home`) and a blocks place (`graview-shipped-lens`).

1. **Give a block a name a face can claim.** Any block may say `key: "fixtures"` (unsaid, its sort and place: `list.2`): the name a face claims it by (`BlockSlots`, see `graview-pages`), never its words.

1. **Work a value out; never store it.** A value that follows from others is declared once, never kept in step by hand. `computed` names it and says it in the rule language:

```ts computed: { net: { expr: "sum(out('includes'), list * units) * (100 - either(first(all('party') where role == 'client').discount, 0)) / 100", label: "After the discount" }, } ```

Every template, view spec, rule, sum and sort reads `net` like a field (`{ field: "net", as: "money" }`, `sort(all('package'), [standing, net], 'desc')`); no act or edit form offers it, and an act that sets one is refused (`computed-written`). It is worked out over the graph the reader holds, so a seat is served one from what it may see. A glance may name one; a `label` or `describe` only one worked out from the record alone (no graph is in hand). A document's top-level `computed` holds facts of the whole graph, read as `fact('name')`; a kind's is changed with `set-computed`. A computed value may be words or a moment, not only a number: `heading: "concat(name, ' · ', format(day, 'EEE d MMM'))"` and `startsAt: "datetime(day, '09:30')"` build a title and a start time (with `addMinutes`, `weekday`, `startOfWeek` beside them), said in the app's `brand.locale` on its `brand.timeZone` — see graview-invariant for the pattern pieces and what `graview check` refuses. `{ expr, format: "percent" }` (or `"money"`, `"duration"`, a `unit`; `set-format` sets it) says it so on its page, cards and CSV; `round(x, 3)` rounds; `hidden: true` keeps a helper off its page, cards and CSV while lists, lenses, rules and views still sort and read by it.

1. **Say counts and times in words.** Templates say counts in words: `{n | words}` ("three"), `{n | plural: 'offer'}` ("offers"), `{out('includes') | and}` ("A, B and C"), `{n | words | capital}` ("Three"), `{at | time}` ("10:47 AM"). A field's label, a group's heading and what an empty list says are words, not templates: braces there would be drawn as typed, and `view-braces` warns of them. A `describe` or `label` written in code is not a template either: say the value in code (`momentAsRead(node.startsAt)`), and `describe-template-in-code` warns of `{field}` returned there.

### Then find out whether it worked

```sh
pnpm build && npx graview check ./dist/domain/app.js
npx graview check --document app.json   # a document
```

Report **the actual output**, including warnings. What it catches here:

- `view-field`, `view-name`, `view-tone` — a view spec naming a field the kind lacks, or a tone outside the kit; `view-key` — two blocks under one key; `view-template`, `view-expression` — a template or a condition it cannot read; `view-depth` — lists nested past three
- `view-whole-text` — a card or row putting a long `text` field whole in a text block, unless it says `lines` (`graview-lists` says how a card shows its start)
- `view-headline-long` — a headline bound to a long `text`, Markdown or long string field whole, which a focus card drew at display size: say it in a `text` block, or head it with `{call|excerpt: 60}` (a headline past about 90 characters is drawn a step smaller and clamped to four lines)
- `computed-cycle` — values worked out from each other; `computed-clash` — a computed name that is already a field; `computed-cost` — work that grows with the cube of the graph (a warning at the square)

Then look: `graview describe <entry> --place <slug>` says each record's card and row as the page draws them, and the page itself shows the blocks in both schemes. Open it as a seat that may not see a listed record: the list is shorter, and the computed value is worked out without it.

### What the check cannot see

- Whether the card says what a person glancing at it needs. The check holds a spec to the vocabulary; only reading the cards on a full list says whether they are the right few facts.
- Whether a computed value is the RIGHT sum. The check proves it terminates and is affordable; work one record out by hand and compare.

---

Say how a Graview kind's card, row and page read, as data — blocks from a closed set bound by {field} templates and rule-language conditions, headlines, figures and lists of related records — and the values worked out from others (computed) that they show, verified by graview check and the page rather than by assuming the spec drew.

The page: https://graview.dev/docs/skills/graview-view-specs.html · Every Graview docs page, for a model: https://graview.dev/llms.txt

---

Source: https://graview.dev/docs/skills/graview-visitor-forms.html

# graview-visitor-forms

`graview-visitor-forms` is one of Graview's 30 authoring skills: instructions an AI coding assistant such as Claude Code or Codex reads before it changes a Graview app. What it teaches: Open one act of a Graview app to people who never join it — an RSVP, a sign-up, a request — as a form drawn alone, run as a visitor the host mints per answer, its answers landing as records and nothing else of the app shown — verified by graview check and by opening the form as that visitor.

Installed into a project by `graview skills install .`, and read by whichever assistant is working beside you.

## The skill

## A form for a visitor

An RSVP link is a page with nothing on it but the question. The visitor has no account, sees no record, and their answer lands as one. Graview does not add a second permission system for it: a visitor is a principal like any other, holding one role, and the policy says what that role may do and see. The form is the declaration of which act, which fields, and what they are told afterwards.

### Do this

1. **Declare the form.** In code (`defineApp({ …, forms })`) or a document's `forms`:

```json "forms": { "rsvp": { "act": "add-guest", "title": "RSVP", "intro": "Tell us whether you can come on June 14.", "fields": ["name", "email", "coming", "note"], "say": "The hosts will write to you a week before." } } ```

`act` makes a record or acts on none — a visitor is shown no record to pick. `fields` is the order asked; unsaid, every argument a visitor could fill, its name first and then what must be answered. `say` is what the visitor reads under "Received — thank you." `submit` is the button (the act's title, unsaid). `role` is the role the visitor holds: `visitor`, unsaid.

1. **Grant the role the act, and name it in no sight.**

```json "policy": { "grants": [{ "roles": ["host"], "mutations": "*" }, { "roles": ["visitor"], "mutations": ["add-guest"] }], "sees": [{ "roles": ["host"], "kinds": ["guest", "table"] }] } ```

A policy with `sees` keeps every kind it does not name from every role it does not name, so the visitor is served nothing — not the guests already there, not the one they just made. A picker the form asks with offers only what the visitor is served: show them a kind by a sight naming their role when they must pick one (an event to answer for).

1. **Mint a visitor per answer, on the host.** `formVisitor(app, "rsvp", "form:<token>")` from `@graview/core/forms` is `{ kind: "visitor", id, name: "a visitor via the RSVP form", roles: ["visitor"] }`: hand it to the store that judges the act (a served store believes it from the seat's headers), so Activity names the answer for the form and never by its token.

1. **Draw it alone.** `@graview/embed/form`:

```ts import { mount } from "@graview/embed/form"; mount(el, { app, form: "rsvp", principal: "form:<token>", remote, height: "100dvh" }); ```

`remote` is `openRemote` opened as the same visitor. No bar, no lists, no seat; `onSubmitted` is told once it is received. A React host draws `VisitorFormPage` from `@graview/pages/visitor-form`.

1. **Try it locally.** `graview preview <document>` serves each form at `/forms/<name>`, a visitor minted per page: open the form's address as it prints it, which carries the run's key.

### Worked examples

- `packages/core/tests/document/fixtures/rsvp.gdd.json` — the RSVP: a form, its grant, a sight that never names the visitor
- `packages/core/tests/unit/a-form-for-a-visitor.test.ts` — the visitor minted, the act run as them, their seat served nothing, every finding
- `packages/embed/tests/unit/a-visitor-answers-a-form-mounted-alone.test.tsx` — the mount, drawn alone and answered

### Then find out whether it worked

```sh
npx graview check ./app.gdd.json
```

A form is held to what a visitor can do: `form-unknown-act`, `form-act-on-a-record`, `form-without-sight` (no policy, or one that says nothing of who sees what: the visitor would be served every record), `form-act-not-granted`, `form-field-unknown`, `form-omits-required`, `form-field-unfillable` (a required picker over records the visitor is not served, or a field their sight keeps from them); and as warnings, `form-visitor-sees` (a sight serves the visitor a kind — to everybody, or by name where no picker asks for it) and `form-visitor-may-more` (the role may run acts no form opens). Report what it said.

**Read what it asks.** `describe_place` with `forms/<name>` (or `graview describe <entry> --place forms/<name>`) says each field in the order asked: its label, a star where it must be answered, what it takes and its choices — as the visitor is asked it.

**And try it.** Open `/forms/<name>` under `graview preview`, answer, and read the store as the host: the record is there, its author "a visitor via the … form". Then read `store.seenBy(visitor).snapshot()` — it should be empty — and the answers the page was sent should name no record.

### What the check cannot see

- Abuse. How many answers one link may take, from where, and whether a token is spent once: the host's, before it mints a visitor.
- Who may open the form at all, and on which plan: the host's.
- Whether the words help. `intro` and `say` are the app's; whether a stranger understands what they are signing up for is a reading, not a check.

---

Open one act of a Graview app to people who never join it — an RSVP, a sign-up, a request — as a form drawn alone, run as a visitor the host mints per answer, its answers landing as records and nothing else of the app shown — verified by graview check and by opening the form as that visitor.

The page: https://graview.dev/docs/skills/graview-visitor-forms.html · Every Graview docs page, for a model: https://graview.dev/llms.txt

---

Source: https://graview.dev/docs/skills/graview-worker-view.html

# graview-worker-view

`graview-worker-view` is one of Graview's 30 authoring skills: instructions an AI coding assistant such as Claude Code or Codex reads before it changes a Graview app. What it teaches: Write a Graview worker view — one plain script, no imports and no build, that draws HTML, SVG and CSS for a kind or the home through the graview global — with a manifest the host enforces, and prove it runs rather than assuming it does.

Installed into a project by `graview skills install .`, and read by whichever assistant is working beside you.

## The skill

## A worker view

A worker view is for what the declared blocks cannot draw: a chart, a grid of cards, a front page with a figure and a ring. It is one plain script. The host runs it in a hardened worker with no network, no storage and no DOM of its own, and draws what it says into a shadow root inside a region the host owns. **What it may draw is broad; what it may reach is not.** Write it against one global, `graview`. There is nothing to import and nothing to build; the word `import` may not appear in it at all, even in a comment, and nor may `export`.

### The manifest

Every view comes with a manifest the host enforces:

```js
{ name: "packages", title: "The packages", attach: "package", cardinality: "many",
  reads: { kinds: ["offer"], edges: ["includes"] },
  acts: ["set-summary", { act: "set-standing", as: "recommend", constants: { standing: "recommended" } }] }
```

- `name` is lower-case letters, digits and hyphens. Acts are recorded `via: "view:<name>"`.
- `title` makes it a named place on both faces, with the slug `placeSlug(title)` (`"the-packages"`).
- A view is as tall as it draws, measured by the host: set no height. On Pages it flows with the page. On the Scene it is a card held to its box, no scrolling: a fade and More at its foot where cut, Open to its page. `flows: false` keeps a frame on Pages; `scene: { maxHeight }` holds the card lower (80–4000px).
- `attach` is a kind, or `"home"` for the front page's body (cardinality `many`).
- `reads` lists the other kinds and the edges it is shown. Nothing else is handed to it.
- `acts` lists the acts it may ask for, by name. An entry with `as` and `constants` is another name for the same act with arguments the view cannot change.
- A view of one record (`cardinality: "one"`) is drawn above the kind's page blocks and the record's own fields, which stay editable. `replaces: "page"` draws it alone, and the page blocks never (`graview-view-specs`). On a view of many, it is its kind's list page (`/<plural>`).
- `gestures: true` lets it hear a wheel, a drag and a pinch (below). `bleed: true` draws it edge to edge on a phone (`graview-view-drawing`).
- `pictures: true` hands each picture on a record with an address the host made from its bytes, never its path, and lets the view place a record's video and open the host's full-screen viewer (`graview-view-drawing`). They share 12 MB: name the kinds it draws, `["circuit"]`, or fields, `{ circuit: "photo" }`.

A manifest that names a kind, an edge or an act the app does not declare is refused before the view starts.

### The global

```js
graview.style(css)              // a stylesheet, after any before it
graview.onProps((props) => …)   // every push of what it is shown (and at once)
graview.props                   // the last push
graview.render(markup)          // draw: a string, graview.html`…`, or nodes
graview.html`<li>${x}</li>`     // markup; every value put in is escaped
graview.on("click", ".card", (event) => …)   // also input, change, keydown, toggle, acted
graview.act(name, args)         // ask for an act: resolves { ok, intent } or { ok: false, reason, message }
graview.navigate("offer:7")     // a record, else a place or a kind's list by slug
graview.navigate({ place: "features", where: { stage: "building" }, section: "Shipping soon" })
```

`props` holds `node`, the record a view of one is drawn for, and `nodes`, the records a view of many is drawn for and those it reads. A record is plain data: `id`, `kind`, `label`, and each field and computed value by name (`props.node.draft`), as the viewer sees it; no `fields` key. A view of one finds its record in `node`, never in `nodes`. A choice holds its option's id; draw the label `props.choices` gives by kind, field and option: `props.choices.actor.motive[node.motive]`. Then `edges` (`{ kind, from, to }` among them), `label` (its title), `acts` (`{ name, title }`, those the viewer may run), `places` (`{ as, title }`), and `theme` (`scheme`, `accent`, `ink`, `radius` …, the app's `name` and `logo`), and `locale` and `timeZone`: say a kept instant with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat(props.locale, { timeZone: props.timeZone, hour: "numeric", minute: "2-digit" })`, the clock the rest of the app says it on, never a zone of your own. `render` keeps what it can, by element and by `data-key` or `id`, so give repeated rows a `data-key`: a field being typed in keeps its text across a push. An event carries `value`, `checked`, `key`, `pressed` for a bound press, and `element`, what the selector matched: read its `data-*`. Elements lack `closest`, `matches` and `dataset`.

### Links and buttons, by default

To go somewhere, `<a data-record>` or `<a data-place>`; to do something, a `<button>` (`data-act` to run an act). Style either freely: the host resets both to the words around them, and your class wins. A `<div>` or `<span>` with only `graview.on("click")` is reached by no keyboard and named nothing; with `role="button"` (checkbox, switch, tab, `aria-pressed`, `aria-expanded`) the host gives it the keyboard and hears Enter or Space as a click. The keyboard shows the host's ring: restyle it with `--graview-focus-color`, never `outline: none`. `class="graview-sr"` is words for a screen reader alone; an `<svg>` with no role, `aria-label` or `<title>` is hidden from one.

### Gestures

With `gestures: true`, `graview.on("wheel" | "drag" | "pinch", selector, fn)` hears them over what the selector matches, at most once a frame with the deltas summed. Each carries `x`, `y` from the matched element's top left and its `width`, `height`; a `wheel` adds `deltaX`, `deltaY`, `deltaMode`, `ctrlKey`, `metaKey`, a `drag` `phase`, `pointerId`, `button`, `pressure`, `dx`, `dy`, a `pinch` (a trackpad's Control-wheel too) `phase`, `scale`, `rotation`. The page scrolls everywhere else; say `touch-action: none` on what drags. Without the flag the check says so.

HTML, SVG and stylesheets, drawn with the app's `--graview-*` tokens so light and dark follow the app's toggle; nothing that loads or escapes. What the host keeps, the tokens, and the only images a view may show (the app's logo, the app's own images, the pictures on records) are `graview-view-drawing`. What the host leaves out it lists in `refused`. A `<section aria-labelledby="h">` is named by its own `<h2 id="h">`; `summary::marker` and `::-webkit-details-marker` style a disclosure's triangle.

### Links

`<a data-record="offer:7">`, `<a data-place="the-packages">` and a whole card or row with `data-record` are links the host follows on a click, a phone's tap and Enter, to what the viewer may see. An `<a href>` goes out only to an address a record was handed. A card, a link out, what a tap inside it reaches, and going narrowed or to a section are `graview-view-links`.

### Writes

An act must be in the manifest. Where every member sees every record, `graview.act` applies it as given; anywhere else **only a press applies an act**: a person's click on a `data-act`, or a field of theirs that saves. How those are written and heard is `graview-view-forms`.

### Limits

About 256 kB of source, 5 000 drawn nodes, 120 messages a second, 1 000 ms per push, and 100 ms a second of the page's time drawing it. Past any, the view is stopped and its records' plain face drawn instead, with why. Draw summaries, not every row of a huge set. Timers between pushes are not timed per push, and a worker kept busy under the heartbeat's 5 s spends the person's CPU: never spin.

### Worked examples

`examples/offers-list.js` is a list lens: rows linking to their records, and a note typed and pressed in. `examples/front-page.js` is a home: a headline, a figure, an SVG ring and cards linking to a place. `examples/a-record.js` is a view of one record: a deliverable's draft read off `props.node`, and "Edit draft" prefilled. `examples/a-map-that-pans-and-zooms.js` is an SVG map whose viewBox a wheel and a pinch zoom around the pointer and a drag pans. Each opens with its manifest.

### Registering it

```ts
import { registerWorkerView, workerHome } from "@graview/guest/host/views";
views: (schema, registry) => registerWorkerView(registry, { manifest, worker: { source } }),
pages.surface("home", workerHome({ manifest: front, worker: { source: frontSource } }));
```

A view with `attach: "home"` given to `registerWorkerView` is the home's own view: the routed home's body, the page the app opens on — full width under the bar on a desk too — and the app's declared home is drawn if it fails. A host with many views hands each one's code as a function (`worker: () => fetch(url).then((r) => r.text()).then((source) => ({ source }))`): the manifest registers the place, and the code is fetched only when the view is first drawn.

### Then find out whether it worked

1. `graview check` the app the view names: a manifest is only as sound as the declaration it reads. `checkManifest(manifest, store)` and `checkViewSource(source)` from `@graview/guest/host/views` must both say nothing.
2. Run it headless, with no network, as a member who may see less than you, over a seed: `graview view check view.js --app <app> --manifest manifest.json --seed <seed.json> --roles <role>`. It prints what the view drew, said as `graview describe` says a place, or why it will not do: `error` (what it threw), `nodes`, `flood`, `slow`, `act` (an act its manifest does not name), `manifest` or `source`. A view of one record runs over the first of its kind the seat sees, or the one `--record <id>` names. In code, `runWorkerViewHeadless` from `@graview/guest/headless` does the same in an isolate you supply.
3. Open the place on both faces as that member. Is anything shown that they should not see? Does the region carry no `data-worker-view-failed`? `start` there means it never ran: the note under the plain face names what the page's Content-Security-Policy lacks (`worker-src blob:`).
4. Toggle the app to dark. Does the view restyle?
5. Follow each link, and tap each card on a phone, as `graview-view-links` says. A view that writes is pressed as `graview-view-forms` says.

### What the check cannot see

`graview check` judges the declaration, not the script. It cannot see a view that throws on an empty graph, draws the wrong number, or takes too long on a big one. Only running it does: `graview view check` on an empty app, a full one, and a member with narrow sight. A headless run is one push with timers that never fire, and nothing laid out, so it cannot see an animation or a layout that breaks at 390; the faces can. Nor can it see a view that misleads. The host keeps it from reaching or leaking anything, not from arranging what the person may see badly.

---

Write a Graview worker view — one plain script, no imports and no build, that draws HTML, SVG and CSS for a kind or the home through the graview global — with a manifest the host enforces, and prove it runs rather than assuming it does.

The page: https://graview.dev/docs/skills/graview-worker-view.html · Every Graview docs page, for a model: https://graview.dev/llms.txt

---

Source: https://graview.dev/docs/recipes.html

# Recipes

A recipe is one prompt to hand your agent, with a different task each, and the app an agent made of it. Each is over Larkspur, a made-up repository, and each runs on its page; each page says how it was made.

```sh
Read https://graview.dev/start.md, then turn this repo's docs into a Graview app.
```

## The recipes

- [Your docs, as an app](https://graview.dev/docs/recipes/docs.html): The repository's docs, the modules they cover and who owns each, with every module that has no doc or no owner flagged and the repair offered.
- [Your decisions, as an app](https://graview.dev/docs/recipes/decisions.html): The architecture decision records: what each decided, what it superseded and which modules it affects, with the loose ends flagged.
- [Your dependencies, as an upgrade plan](https://graview.dev/docs/recipes/dependencies.html): Every third-party package, the version pinned against the latest on npm, the modules that use it and the upgrade it needs, with the risky ones flagged.
- [Your architecture, with a face of its own](https://graview.dev/docs/recipes/architecture.html): The zones the modules group into, what each module imports, who owns each zone, and the modules no zone holds yet, with a product face of its own over the running preview.

---

Graview recipes: one prompt to hand an agent, with a different task each, and the app it made, checked on every push and live on its page.

The page: https://graview.dev/docs/recipes.html · Every Graview docs page, for a model: https://graview.dev/llms.txt

---

Source: https://graview.dev/docs/recipes/architecture.html

# Your architecture, with a face of its own

This recipe is one prompt, the app it makes, and the face a team gives that app next. The zones the modules group into, what each module imports, who owns each zone, and the modules no zone holds yet, with a product face of its own over the running preview.

```sh
Read https://graview.dev/start.md, then turn this repo's architecture into a Graview app.
```

Paste it into Claude Code, Codex or Cursor at the root of your repository. [start.md](https://graview.dev/start.md) is the page the agent reads.

## The app, running

This is the declaration below, compiled in your browser by the same compiler `graview check` uses, over the seed below. Press a district; open the problems; take a repair.

*The app the architecture prompt made, live: a live demo, on the HTML page.*

## What the agent declared

**Larkspur architecture**: Larkspur's architecture: the zones its modules group into, what each module imports from the others, who owns each zone, and the modules no zone holds yet. 3 kinds, 9 acts and 2 rules, each rule with the act that repairs it.

| Kind | Fields | Relations | Records in the seed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `zone` | `name`, `summary` | `ownedBy` to `person` | 7 |
| `module` | `path`, `packageName`, `area` | `inZone` to `zone`; `importsFrom` to `module` | 16 |
| `person` | `handle` | none | 7 |

### The rules

- **Every module is in a zone.** Over each module: requires `exists(out('inZone'))`. Repaired by “Put it in a zone” (`put-in-zone`).
- **Every zone has an owner.** Over each zone: requires `exists(out('ownedBy'))`. Repaired by “Give it an owner” (`give-zone-owner`).

## What graview check says

Run on every push, against the committed file:

```sh
npx graview check --document app.json
✓ the document compiles and checks clean
```

## A face of its own

An app worth keeping wants a look and feel of its own before it wants a server. This one keeps the store where `graview preview` runs it, and draws Graview's routed face over it with a shell, a home, a route and a record page in the team's own words: a change made on either page is the other's at once. If it mounts the scene too, give the embed `bar: { faces: false, name: false }` so the face's own shell is the one bar.

```sh
# the store and its own page, on 4800: it prints the address to open, which carries its key
npx graview preview app.json --seed seed.json --port 4800
# the face, over it, on 5173, handed that address
cd face && npm install && GRAVIEW_PREVIEW="http://localhost:4800/?graview_key=…" npm run dev
```

CI runs these files as they are: `pnpm verify face-recipe` installs them over the built packages, starts the preview and the face’s own dev server, and checks that they typecheck, that the preview refuses the face’s page without the proxy and answers it through it, that the face draws its own shell, home and zone page, and that a change on either side reaches the other live.

### `face/package.json`

What it installs: the framework's packages, React and the router, and Vite. No framework source: a product installs the packages.

```json
{
  "name": "larkspur-architecture-face",
  "private": true,
  "type": "module",
  "scripts": {
    "store": "graview preview ../app.json --seed ../seed.json --port 4800",
    "dev": "vite",
    "build": "vite build"
  },
  "dependencies": {
    "@graview/core": "^0.1.41",
    "@graview/pages": "^0.1.41",
    "@graview/primitives": "^0.1.41",
    "@graview/react": "^0.1.41",
    "@graview/ship": "^0.1.41",
    "react": "^19.2.0",
    "react-dom": "^19.2.0",
    "react-router-dom": "^7.1.1"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "graview": "^0.1.41",
    "@types/react": "^19.2.0",
    "@types/react-dom": "^19.2.0",
    "typescript": "^5.7.2",
    "vite": "^5.4.11"
  }
}
```

### `face/vite.config.ts`

The dev server, and its proxy: every `/graview` request, the socket too, goes to the preview, with the preview's own Origin, so its same-app doors answer a page they would refuse from another port.

```typescript
import { defineConfig } from "vite";

/*
 * THE STORE IS THE PREVIEW'S; THE PAGE IS YOURS.
 *
 * `graview preview ../app.json --seed ../seed.json --port 4800` serves the
 * store at /graview/ beside its own page, and prints the address to open:
 * `http://localhost:4800/?graview_key=…`, which carries that run's key. Hand
 * this dev server that address (`GRAVIEW_PREVIEW="…" npm run dev`): it
 * serves your face, and hands every /graview/ request — the socket too —
 * to the preview, with the key.
 *
 * The preview answers only its own page: a request whose Origin is another
 * site is refused, so a page on another port cannot sit in its seat, and
 * nothing without the key is answered at all. Here the page is yours on
 * purpose, so the proxy says the request comes from the preview's own
 * origin, and carries the key, on the HTTP calls and on the socket's
 * upgrade. The key stays here: the page is handed only where the preview is.
 */
const printed = new URL(process.env["GRAVIEW_PREVIEW"] ?? "http://localhost:4800");
const KEY = printed.searchParams.get("graview_key") ?? "";
const PREVIEW = printed.origin;

export default defineConfig({
  esbuild: { jsx: "automatic" },
  // Where the preview's own page is, for a record's link into its scene.
  define: { "import.meta.env.GRAVIEW_PREVIEW": JSON.stringify(PREVIEW) },
  // main.tsx awaits the store at the top level.
  build: { target: "es2022" },
  resolve: { dedupe: ["react", "react-dom", "react-router-dom"] },
  server: {
    port: Number(process.env["PORT"] ?? 5173),
    strictPort: true,
    proxy: {
      "/graview": {
        target: PREVIEW,
        ws: true,
        changeOrigin: true,
        configure(proxy) {
          proxy.on("proxyReq", (request) => {
            request.setHeader("origin", PREVIEW);
            if (KEY) request.setHeader("x-graview-key", KEY);
          });
          proxy.on("proxyReqWs", (request) => {
            request.setHeader("origin", PREVIEW);
            if (KEY) request.setHeader("x-graview-key", KEY);
          });
        },
      },
    },
  },
});
```

### `face/index.html`

The page.

```html
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
    <title>Larkspur architecture</title>
    <style>html, body { margin: 0; } body { background: var(--graview-ground, Canvas); }</style>
  </head>
  <body>
    <div id="root"></div>
    <script type="module" src="/src/main.tsx"></script>
  </body>
</html>
```

### `face/src/main.tsx`

The app and the seat from the preview's `/graview/document`, the store over `openRemote`, live; `themeCss` adopted by hand; the pictures from `registerDeclaredLenses(registerViewSpecs(registerDefaultViews(…)))`; and `PagesApp` with the face's own registry.

```typescript
import type { AnySchema, GraviewApp, Principal } from "@graview/core";
import { appFromOrCompile, sayFindings } from "@graview/core/compiled";
import { PagesApp } from "@graview/pages";
import { createViews } from "@graview/react";
import { registerDeclaredLenses, registerDefaultViews, registerViewSpecs, themeCss } from "@graview/primitives";
import { openRemote } from "@graview/ship/browser";
import { createRoot } from "react-dom/client";
import { pages, SCENE } from "./pages.js";

/*
 * A PRODUCT FACE OVER A RUNNING PREVIEW'S STORE.
 *
 * The preview holds the store and the declaration; this page is the face.
 * It asks the preview (through the dev server's proxy, vite.config.ts) for
 * the app and the seat it sits in, opens the store over the wire, live, and
 * draws Graview's routed face with its own shell, home, routes and record
 * pages. A change made here is the preview's, and its own page sees it.
 */
const root = document.getElementById("root");
if (!root) throw new Error("no #root");

const handed = (await (await fetch("/graview/document")).json()) as { readonly document: unknown; readonly compiled?: unknown; readonly principal: Principal; readonly state?: unknown };
const compiled = await appFromOrCompile(handed);
if (!compiled.ok) throw new Error(sayFindings(compiled.findings));
const app = compiled.app as GraviewApp<AnySchema>;

const remote = await openRemote({ app, url: window.location.origin, principal: handed.principal, live: true, subprotocol: true, pollMs: 1200, ...(handed.state ? { state: handed.state as never, openTimeoutMs: 0 } : {}) });

/*
 * THE LOOK, ADOPTED BY HAND. The embed would put the theme on its own
 * element; a face of its own puts it on the document, from the app's brand,
 * and switching scheme is one replaceSync.
 */
const sheet = new CSSStyleSheet();
document.adoptedStyleSheets = [sheet];
const scheme = window.matchMedia?.("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches ? "dark" : "light";
sheet.replaceSync(themeCss(scheme, app.brand));
document.documentElement.dataset["graviewScheme"] = scheme;
document.title = app.name;

/*
 * THE PICTURES: every kind at every fidelity from the declaration, the
 * record pages it declares as blocks, and its titled lenses as places.
 */
const views = registerDeclaredLenses(registerViewSpecs(registerDefaultViews(app.schema, createViews(app.schema)), app.schema, app.viewSpecs), app);

createRoot(root).render(
  <PagesApp
    context={{
      store: remote.store,
      principal: handed.principal,
      ...(app.brand ? { brand: app.brand } : {}),
      // A record's "See it on the map" opens the preview's own scene, focused on it.
      sceneHref: SCENE,
      views,
      settings: app.settings ?? [],
      app,
    }}
    registry={pages(app)}
  />,
);
// What a harness waits on, rather than a timer and a hope.
Object.assign(window, { __graview: { store: remote.store, principal: handed.principal }, __faceReady: true });
```

### `face/src/pages.tsx`

The face's own shell (with Find and Undo in its own row), home, a route about no one kind, and a zone's record page whose map link is `spatialHref(id, sceneHref)` into the preview's own scene. Every other page is still derived.

```typescript
import type { AnySchema, GraviewApp } from "@graview/core";
import {
  createPageRegistry,
  PageFind,
  PageMain,
  pageStyles,
  PageUndo,
  recordFacts,
  recordPath,
  Repairs,
  spatialHref,
  useStoreTick,
  type PageComponent,
  type PageContext,
} from "@graview/pages";
import type { ReactNode } from "react";
import { Link, NavLink, useParams } from "react-router-dom";

type S = AnySchema;
type Page = PageComponent<S>;

/** The preview's own page, where its scene lives: a record's "See it on the map" goes there. */
const PREVIEW = (import.meta as { env?: Record<string, string | undefined> }).env?.["GRAVIEW_PREVIEW"] ?? "http://localhost:4800";
export const SCENE = `${PREVIEW}/places/overview`;

interface Zone {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly kind: string;
  readonly name: string;
  readonly summary?: string;
}

/** Every zone, its modules and its owners, read off the graph as this seat sees it. */
function zonesOf(context: PageContext<S>) {
  const graph = context.principal ? context.store.seenBy(context.principal).graph : context.store.graph;
  const edges = graph.allEdges();
  return (graph.nodesOfKind("zone" as never) as unknown as Zone[]).map((zone) => ({
    zone,
    modules: edges.filter((edge) => edge.kind === "inZone" && edge.to === zone.id).map((edge) => graph.getNode(edge.from)!),
    owners: edges.filter((edge) => edge.kind === "ownedBy" && edge.from === zone.id).map((edge) => graph.getNode(edge.to)!),
  }));
}

/** THE FRAME AROUND EVERY ROUTE: the app's name, the team's own words for where to go, and Find and Undo in its own row. */
function Shell({ context, children }: { context: PageContext<S>; children: ReactNode }) {
  useStoreTick(context.store);
  const problems = context.store.violations().length;
  const link = ({ isActive }: { isActive: boolean }) => ({ ...pageStyles.link, fontWeight: isActive ? 650 : 450 });
  return (
    <div style={{ minHeight: "100dvh", display: "grid", gridTemplateRows: "auto 1fr" }}>
      <header data-testid="face-shell" style={{ display: "flex", flexWrap: "wrap", alignItems: "center", gap: 16, padding: "12px 20px", borderBottom: "1px solid var(--graview-edge)" }}>
        <strong style={{ fontFamily: "var(--graview-font-display)" }}>{context.app?.name ?? "Architecture"}</strong>
        <nav aria-label="Where to go" style={{ display: "flex", gap: 14 }}>
          <NavLink to="/" end style={link}>Zones</NavLink>
          <NavLink to="/modules" style={link}>Modules</NavLink>
          <NavLink to="/owners" style={link}>Owners</NavLink>
          <NavLink to="/problems" style={link}>{problems > 0 ? `Problems (${problems})` : "Problems"}</NavLink>
        </nav>
        <span style={{ flex: 1 }} />
        <PageFind context={context} />
        <PageUndo context={context} />
      </header>
      {children}
    </div>
  );
}

/** THE HOME: every zone as a card, its modules counted and who owns it said. */
function Home({ context }: { context: PageContext<S> }) {
  useStoreTick(context.store);
  return (
    <PageMain context={context} data-testid="face-home">
      <h1 style={pageStyles.h1}>Zones</h1>
      <ul style={{ listStyle: "none", margin: 0, padding: 0, display: "grid", gap: 12, gridTemplateColumns: "repeat(auto-fill, minmax(16rem, 1fr))" }}>
        {zonesOf(context).map(({ zone, modules, owners }) => (
          <li key={zone.id} data-zone={zone.id} style={{ ...pageStyles.rule, display: "grid", gap: 4 }}>
            <Link to={recordPath(context.store.schema, "zone", zone.id)} style={pageStyles.link}>
              <strong>{zone.name}</strong>
            </Link>
            <span style={pageStyles.quiet}>{modules.length === 1 ? "1 module" : `${modules.length} modules`} · {owners.length === 0 ? "no owner" : owners.map((owner) => String(owner["handle"])).join(", ")}</span>
          </li>
        ))}
      </ul>
    </PageMain>
  );
}

/** A ROUTE ABOUT NO ONE KIND: who owns what, by person. */
function Owners({ context }: { context: PageContext<S> }) {
  useStoreTick(context.store);
  const zones = zonesOf(context);
  const people = context.store.graph.nodesOfKind("person" as never) as unknown as { id: string; handle: string }[];
  return (
    <PageMain context={context} data-testid="face-owners">
      <h1 style={pageStyles.h1}>Owners</h1>
      <dl style={{ display: "grid", gap: 8 }}>
        {people.map((person) => (
          <div key={person.id}>
            <dt><strong>{person.handle}</strong></dt>
            <dd style={{ margin: 0 }}>{zones.filter(({ owners }) => owners.some((owner) => owner.id === person.id)).map(({ zone }) => zone.name).join(", ") || "Owns no zone"}</dd>
          </div>
        ))}
      </dl>
    </PageMain>
  );
}

/** A ZONE'S PAGE in the team's words: what it is for, its owners, its modules, and what the rules say is missing, with the repair. */
function ZonePage({ context }: { context: PageContext<S> }) {
  const { store, principal } = context;
  useStoreTick(store);
  const id = decodeURIComponent(useParams()["id"] ?? "");
  const facts = recordFacts(store, id, principal ? { principal } : {});
  const found = zonesOf(context).find(({ zone }) => zone.id === id);
  if (!facts || !found) {
    return (
      <PageMain context={context}>
        <h1 style={pageStyles.h1}>No zone lives at this address.</h1>
      </PageMain>
    );
  }
  return (
    <PageMain context={context} data-testid="zone-page">
      <p style={pageStyles.eyebrow}>Zone</p>
      <h1 style={pageStyles.h1}>{found.zone.name}</h1>
      {found.zone.summary ? <p style={pageStyles.lede}>{found.zone.summary}</p> : null}
      <a href={spatialHref(id, context.sceneHref)} style={{ ...pageStyles.link, ...pageStyles.quiet }} data-testid="spatial-link">
        See it on the map ↗
      </a>
      {facts.violations.map((violation, index) => (
        <section key={index} style={{ ...pageStyles.rule, display: "grid", gap: 8 }} data-testid="zone-problem">
          <p style={{ margin: 0, color: "var(--graview-warn)", fontWeight: 550 }}>{violation.message}</p>
          <Repairs<S> store={store} repairs={violation.repairs} {...(principal ? { principal } : {})} />
        </section>
      ))}
      <h2 style={pageStyles.h2}>Owned by</h2>
      <p>{found.owners.map((owner) => String(owner["handle"])).join(", ") || "No one yet."}</p>
      <h2 style={pageStyles.h2}>Modules</h2>
      <ul data-testid="zone-modules">
        {found.modules.map((module) => (
          <li key={module.id}>
            <Link to={recordPath(store.schema, "module", module.id)} style={pageStyles.link}>
              {String(module["path"])}
            </Link>
          </li>
        ))}
      </ul>
    </PageMain>
  );
}

/** Your pages over the derived ones: every other kind's list and record, the problems page and the forms are still Graview's. */
export function pages(app: GraviewApp<S>) {
  return createPageRegistry<S, Page>(app.schema)
    .surface("shell", Shell, { without: ["find", "undo"] })
    .surface("home", Home as Page)
    .register("zone", "record", ZonePage as Page)
    .route("/owners", Owners as Page);
}
```

### `face/tsconfig.json`

Strict, for the bundler.

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2022",
    "lib": ["ES2022", "DOM", "DOM.Iterable"],
    "module": "ESNext",
    "moduleResolution": "Bundler",
    "jsx": "react-jsx",
    "strict": true,
    "noUncheckedIndexedAccess": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true,
    "noEmit": true,
    "isolatedModules": true,
    "verbatimModuleSyntax": true
  },
  "include": ["src"]
}
```

## How it was made

Claude Code wrote the declaration and the seed from Larkspur's package.json files and CODEOWNERS, the way the prompt asks, and then the face under face/ by hand from the framework's own pieces, over graview preview of those two files. Nothing here was run from the prompt alone.

CI does not run an agent. On every push it checks the committed declaration with `graview check --document`, loads the seed into a store, and opens this page in a browser to see the app mount. To run the prompt again yourself:

```sh
node scripts/fixtures/recipes/larkspur.mjs larkspur
cd larkspur && git init -q && git add -A && git commit -qm larkspur
# then paste the prompt into your agent
```

The files: [`app.json`](https://graview.dev/recipes/architecture/app.json) and [`seed.json`](https://graview.dev/recipes/architecture/seed.json) (30 records and 46 relations).

## The declaration, in full

```json
{
  "format": "graview-document",
  "formatVersion": 1,
  "name": "Larkspur architecture",
  "description": "Larkspur's architecture: the zones its modules group into, what each module imports from the others, who owns each zone, and the modules no zone holds yet.",
  "roles": [
    "engineer"
  ],
  "policy": {
    "grants": [
      {
        "roles": [
          "engineer"
        ],
        "mutations": "*"
      }
    ]
  },
  "kinds": {
    "zone": {
      "noun": "zone",
      "plural": "zones",
      "label": "{name}",
      "description": "A part of the codebase that changes together: the modules one team reviews as one.",
      "fields": {
        "name": {
          "type": "string",
          "required": true,
          "description": "What the team calls it."
        },
        "summary": {
          "type": "string",
          "description": "What it is for, in a line."
        }
      },
      "edges": {
        "ownedBy": {
          "to": [
            "person"
          ],
          "cardinality": "many",
          "description": "who reviews its modules",
          "inverse": "the zones they own"
        }
      }
    },
    "module": {
      "noun": "module",
      "plural": "modules",
      "label": "{path}",
      "description": "A workspace directory with its own package.json, under services/, packages/ or tools/.",
      "fields": {
        "path": {
          "type": "string",
          "required": true,
          "description": "The directory, from the repository root."
        },
        "packageName": {
          "type": "string",
          "label": "Package",
          "description": "The name in its package.json."
        },
        "area": {
          "type": "enum",
          "options": [
            "service",
            "package",
            "tool"
          ],
          "required": true,
          "description": "Which workspace folder it sits in."
        }
      },
      "edges": {
        "inZone": {
          "to": [
            "zone"
          ],
          "cardinality": "one",
          "description": "the zone it belongs to",
          "inverse": "its modules"
        },
        "importsFrom": {
          "to": [
            "module"
          ],
          "cardinality": "many",
          "description": "the modules its package.json depends on",
          "inverse": "the modules that import it"
        }
      },
      "glance": [
        "area",
        "packageName"
      ]
    },
    "person": {
      "noun": "person",
      "plural": "people",
      "label": "{handle}",
      "description": "Someone .github/CODEOWNERS names.",
      "fields": {
        "handle": {
          "type": "string",
          "required": true,
          "description": "Their handle in CODEOWNERS."
        }
      }
    }
  },
  "acts": {
    "add-zone": {
      "creates": "zone",
      "title": "Add a zone",
      "description": "Record a part of the codebase that changes together."
    },
    "add-module": {
      "creates": "module",
      "title": "Add a module",
      "description": "Record a workspace directory with its own package.json."
    },
    "add-person": {
      "creates": "person",
      "title": "Add a person",
      "description": "Record someone CODEOWNERS names."
    },
    "give-zone-owner": {
      "on": "zone",
      "connects": "ownedBy",
      "title": "Give the zone an owner",
      "description": "Say who reviews this zone's modules.",
      "fromTheOtherEnd": "Give them a zone"
    },
    "take-zone-owner": {
      "on": "zone",
      "severs": "ownedBy",
      "title": "Take an owner off the zone",
      "description": "Say this person no longer reviews this zone.",
      "fromTheOtherEnd": "Take a zone off them"
    },
    "put-in-zone": {
      "on": "module",
      "connects": "inZone",
      "title": "Put it in a zone",
      "description": "Say which zone this module belongs to.",
      "fromTheOtherEnd": "Put a module in this zone"
    },
    "take-out-of-zone": {
      "on": "module",
      "severs": "inZone",
      "title": "Take it out of its zone",
      "description": "Say this module no longer belongs to that zone.",
      "fromTheOtherEnd": "Take a module out of this zone"
    },
    "import-from": {
      "on": "module",
      "connects": "importsFrom",
      "title": "Say what it imports",
      "description": "Name a module its package.json depends on.",
      "fromTheOtherEnd": "Say a module imports this one"
    },
    "stop-importing": {
      "on": "module",
      "severs": "importsFrom",
      "title": "Say it no longer imports one",
      "description": "Take a module off what it depends on.",
      "fromTheOtherEnd": "Say a module no longer imports this one"
    }
  },
  "rules": {
    "module-in-zone": {
      "title": "Every module is in a zone",
      "over": "module",
      "require": "exists(out('inZone'))",
      "says": "{path} is in no zone",
      "repairs": [
        {
          "act": "put-in-zone",
          "label": "Put it in a zone"
        }
      ]
    },
    "zone-has-owner": {
      "title": "Every zone has an owner",
      "over": "zone",
      "require": "exists(out('ownedBy'))",
      "says": "No one owns {name}",
      "repairs": [
        {
          "act": "give-zone-owner",
          "label": "Give it an owner"
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

A Graview recipe: The zones the modules group into, what each module imports, who owns each zone, and the modules no zone holds yet, with a product face of its own over the running preview.

# Your decisions, as an app

This recipe is what an agent made of one prompt, in a repository it had never seen. The architecture decision records: what each decided, what it superseded and which modules it affects, with the loose ends flagged.

```sh
Read https://graview.dev/start.md, then turn this repo's decisions into a Graview app.
```

Paste it into Claude Code, Codex or Cursor at the root of your repository. [start.md](https://graview.dev/start.md) is the page the agent reads.

## The app, running

This is the declaration below, compiled in your browser by the same compiler `graview check` uses, over the seed below. Press a district; open the problems; take a repair.

*The app the decisions prompt made, live: a live demo, on the HTML page.*

## What the agent declared

**Larkspur decisions**: Larkspur's architecture decision records (docs/adr): each decision, its status and date, what superseded it, and the modules it affects. 2 kinds, 8 acts and 6 rules, each rule with the act that repairs it.

| Kind | Fields | Relations | Records in the seed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `decision` | `number`, `title`, `status`, `date`, `file`, `wholeRepository` | `supersededBy` to `decision`; `affects` to `module` | 14 |
| `module` | `path`, `packageName`, `description` | none | 16 |

### The rules

- **A superseded decision names what superseded it.** Over each decision, when `status == 'superseded'`: requires `present(supersededBy)`. Repaired by “Name what superseded it” (`mark-superseded`).
- **A decision something supersedes says so.** Over each decision, when `present(supersededBy)`: requires `status == 'superseded'`. Repaired by “Mark it superseded” (`mark-superseded`) or “It is not superseded” (`unmark-superseded`).
- **What supersedes a decision is accepted.** Over each decision, when `present(supersededBy)`: requires `supersededBy.status == 'accepted'`. Repaired by “It is not superseded” (`unmark-superseded`).
- **A decision is superseded only by a later one.** Over each decision, when `present(supersededBy)`: requires `supersededBy.date >= date`. Repaired by “It is not superseded” (`unmark-superseded`).
- **A proposal is decided within 90 days.** Over each decision, when `status == 'proposed'`: requires `days(date, today()) <= 90`. Repaired by “Accept it” (`accept-decision`) or “Reject it” (`reject-decision`).
- **An accepted decision affects something.** Over each decision, when `status == 'accepted'`: requires `wholeRepository == true or exists(out('affects'))`. Repaired by “Name a module it affects” (`affect-module`).

## What graview check says

Run on every push, against the committed file:

```sh
npx graview check --document app.json
· rules.proposal-not-left-open: Rule "proposal-not-left-open" reads the clock (today(), now(), a computed field that does, or a kind whose records retire on a date), so the day turning breaks or mends it with nothing changed. A store judges it again only when its host ticks it. — Host it with @graview/ship (openStore, serve and openRemote tick at each midnight: the app's, in brand.timeZone, else UTC's), or call store.tick(now) when the day turns — once a day from a host's own alarm, untilTheDayTurns(now, brand.timeZone) ahead — and its subscribers hear what appeared and cleared.
```

A line starting with a dot is a note, not a warning: advice the checker leaves for a person to weigh.

## How it was made

An agent was given the prompt above and nothing else, at the root of Larkspur: a booking service for small clinics that does not exist, written as a TypeScript monorepo the size of a real one, with sixteen modules, guides and runbooks with gaps, a CODEOWNERS that misses some, fourteen decision records and pinned dependencies. It followed [start.md](https://graview.dev/start.md), scaffolded, declared, ran `graview check` until it was clean, opened `graview preview` and reported back. The two files it wrote are committed as they came out of that run.

CI does not run an agent. On every push it checks the committed declaration with `graview check --document`, loads the seed into a store, and opens this page in a browser to see the app mount. To run the prompt again yourself:

```sh
node scripts/fixtures/recipes/larkspur.mjs larkspur
cd larkspur && git init -q && git add -A && git commit -qm larkspur
# then paste the prompt into your agent
```

The files: [`app.json`](https://graview.dev/recipes/decisions/app.json) and [`seed.json`](https://graview.dev/recipes/decisions/seed.json) (30 records and 28 relations).

## The declaration, in full

```json
{
  "format": "graview-document",
  "formatVersion": 1,
  "name": "Larkspur decisions",
  "description": "Larkspur's architecture decision records (docs/adr): each decision, its status and date, what superseded it, and the modules it affects.",
  "kinds": {
    "decision": {
      "noun": "decision",
      "plural": "decisions",
      "label": "ADR {number}: {title}",
      "description": "One numbered record in docs/adr. Never edited after it is accepted; a changed mind is a new record that supersedes the old one.",
      "fields": {
        "number": { "type": "integer", "required": true, "min": 1, "description": "The record's number, from its file name and heading." },
        "title": { "type": "string", "required": true, "description": "The record's heading, without its number." },
        "status": { "type": "enum", "options": ["proposed", "accepted", "rejected", "superseded"], "required": true, "description": "The record's Status line." },
        "date": { "type": "date", "required": true, "description": "The record's Date line." },
        "file": { "type": "string", "required": true, "description": "Where the record lives in the repository." },
        "wholeRepository": { "type": "boolean", "label": "Affects the whole repository", "description": "The record's Affects line says the whole repository rather than naming modules." }
      },
      "edges": {
        "supersededBy": { "to": ["decision"], "cardinality": "one", "description": "the decision that superseded it", "inverse": "the decisions it supersedes" },
        "affects": { "to": ["module"], "cardinality": "many", "description": "the modules it affects", "inverse": "the decisions that affect it" }
      },
      "fieldRoles": { "when": "date" },
      "glance": ["status", "date", "wholeRepository"]
    },
    "module": {
      "noun": "module",
      "plural": "modules",
      "label": "{path}",
      "description": "A workspace package that pnpm-workspace.yaml takes in: a directory under services/, packages/ or tools/ with its own package.json.",
      "fields": {
        "path": { "type": "string", "required": true, "description": "The directory, from the repository root." },
        "packageName": { "type": "string", "required": true, "label": "Package", "description": "The name in its package.json." },
        "description": { "type": "string", "description": "The description in its package.json." }
      }
    }
  },
  "acts": {
    "add-decision": { "creates": "decision", "title": "Record a decision", "description": "Add a decision record from docs/adr." },
    "add-module": { "creates": "module", "title": "Add a module", "description": "Record a workspace package." },
    "affect-module": { "on": "decision", "connects": "affects", "title": "Say it affects a module", "description": "Name a module this decision affects.", "fromTheOtherEnd": "Name a decision that affects it" },
    "unaffect-module": { "on": "decision", "severs": "affects", "title": "Say it no longer affects a module", "description": "Take a module off this decision's Affects line.", "fromTheOtherEnd": "Take a decision off it" },
    "mark-superseded": { "on": "decision", "connects": "supersededBy", "sets": { "status": "superseded" }, "title": "Name what superseded it", "description": "Name the decision that superseded this one, and mark it superseded.", "fromTheOtherEnd": "Name a decision it supersedes" },
    "unmark-superseded": { "on": "decision", "severs": "supersededBy", "sets": { "status": "accepted" }, "title": "It is not superseded", "description": "Take back what superseded this decision, and mark it accepted again.", "fromTheOtherEnd": "Take back a decision it supersedes" },
    "accept-decision": { "on": "decision", "sets": { "status": "accepted" }, "title": "Accept it", "description": "Mark the decision accepted." },
    "reject-decision": { "on": "decision", "sets": { "status": "rejected" }, "title": "Reject it", "description": "Mark the decision rejected: it was considered and not taken." }
  },
  "rules": {
    "superseded-names-successor": {
      "title": "A superseded decision names what superseded it",
      "over": "decision",
      "when": "status == 'superseded'",
      "require": "present(supersededBy)",
      "says": "ADR {number} is superseded but does not say by what",
      "repairs": [{ "act": "mark-superseded", "label": "Name what superseded it" }]
    },
    "successor-is-marked-superseded": {
      "title": "A decision something supersedes says so",
      "over": "decision",
      "when": "present(supersededBy)",
      "require": "status == 'superseded'",
      "says": "ADR {number} has a successor but its status is {status}",
      "repairs": [{ "act": "mark-superseded", "label": "Mark it superseded" }, { "act": "unmark-superseded", "label": "It is not superseded" }]
    },
    "successor-is-accepted": {
      "title": "What supersedes a decision is accepted",
      "over": "decision",
      "when": "present(supersededBy)",
      "require": "supersededBy.status == 'accepted'",
      "says": "ADR {number} is superseded by a decision that is not accepted",
      "repairs": [{ "act": "unmark-superseded", "label": "It is not superseded" }]
    },
    "successor-is-newer": {
      "title": "A decision is superseded only by a later one",
      "over": "decision",
      "when": "present(supersededBy)",
      "require": "supersededBy.date >= date",
      "says": "ADR {number} is superseded by a decision dated before it",
      "repairs": [{ "act": "unmark-superseded", "label": "It is not superseded" }]
    },
    "proposal-not-left-open": {
      "title": "A proposal is decided within 90 days",
      "over": "decision",
      "when": "status == 'proposed'",
      "require": "days(date, today()) <= 90",
      "says": "ADR {number} has been proposed since {date} and is still open",
      "repairs": [{ "act": "accept-decision", "label": "Accept it" }, { "act": "reject-decision", "label": "Reject it" }]
    },
    "accepted-affects-something": {
      "title": "An accepted decision affects something",
      "over": "decision",
      "when": "status == 'accepted'",
      "require": "wholeRepository == true or exists(out('affects'))",
      "says": "ADR {number} is accepted but names no module it affects",
      "repairs": [{ "act": "affect-module", "label": "Name a module it affects" }]
    }
  }
}
```

# Your dependencies, as an upgrade plan

This recipe is what an agent made of one prompt, in a repository it had never seen. Every third-party package, the version pinned against the latest on npm, the modules that use it and the upgrade it needs, with the risky ones flagged.

```sh
Read https://graview.dev/start.md, then turn this repo's dependencies into a Graview app.
```

Paste it into Claude Code, Codex or Cursor at the root of your repository. [start.md](https://graview.dev/start.md) is the page the agent reads.

## The app, running

This is the declaration below, compiled in your browser by the same compiler `graview check` uses, over the seed below. Press a district; open the problems; take a repair.

*The app the dependencies prompt made, live: a live demo, on the HTML page.*

## What the agent declared

**Dependencies**: Larkspur's third-party packages: the version each package.json pins, the latest on npm, which modules use each, and the upgrade each needs. 5 kinds, 24 acts and 3 rules, each rule with the act that repairs it.

| Kind | Fields | Relations | Records in the seed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `module` | `path`, `name`, `summary` | `ownedBy` to `person` | 17 |
| `person` | `handle` | none | 7 |
| `package` | `name`, `pinned`, `latest`, `upgrade`, `plan` | `assignedTo` to `person` | 35 |
| `dependency` | `name`, `version`, `section`, `manifest` | `declaredIn` to `module`; `pins` to `package` | 49 |
| `decision` | `number`, `title`, `status`, `date`, `file` | `affects` to `module`; `supersedes` to `decision`; `drops` to `package` | 14 |

### The rules

- **One version per package.** Over each dependency: requires `version == pins.pinned`. Repaired by “Pin it like the others” (`align-pin`).
- **A major upgrade has someone on it.** Over each package, when `upgrade == 'major' && plan != 'drop'`: requires `present(assignedTo)`. Repaired by “Assign its upgrade” (`assign-upgrade`).
- **What an accepted decision drops is planned to go.** Over each package, when `some(in('drops'), status == 'accepted')`: requires `plan == 'drop'`. Repaired by “Plan to drop it” (`plan-drop`).

## What graview check says

Run on every push, against the committed file:

```sh
npx graview check --document app.json
✓ the document compiles and checks clean
```

## How it was made

An agent was given the prompt above and nothing else, at the root of Larkspur: a booking service for small clinics that does not exist, written as a TypeScript monorepo the size of a real one, with sixteen modules, guides and runbooks with gaps, a CODEOWNERS that misses some, fourteen decision records and pinned dependencies. It followed [start.md](https://graview.dev/start.md), scaffolded, declared, ran `graview check` until it was clean, opened `graview preview` and reported back. The two files it wrote are committed as they came out of that run.
